verdict.rationale: Linear's own changelog says Linear Agent runs the application, tests it in the browser, navigates through a flow to verify its implementation, and captures before-and-after screenshots for review alongside the code. This covers every element of the story, but only through short changelog announcements. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation (e.g. how screenshots are surfaced, which app types are supported) and independent or hands-on corroboration that the verification and screenshot capture work in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent verify its own implementation by navigating the app and capturing before-and-after screenshots

citations.quote: The agent opens the app, navigates through a flow, and verifies its implementation. It also captures before-and-after screenshots
It also captures before-and-after screenshots, making visual changes easier to review alongside the code.
Once the application is running, Linear Agent tests its work where users experience it: in the browser.
Linear Agent can now set up, run, and test your code before returning its work.
